claim: In Expanse v3, a male-CNS core with the real type-to-type wiring and learned Dale-preserving edge strengths reaches lower held-out loss than the same core on a degree-preserving, sign- and role-stratified shuffle of that wiring.

protocol.notes: Full male-CNS type graph (11,751 types, 3,830,931 edges). Only the lab core trains; trunk frozen (v3). Every arm starts from the same function (gate 0) with the same seed-determined core init, rows, order and schedule.

notes: FlyGPT's question at Expanse scale. The shuffle keeps every type's in-degree, out-degree, self-loop and multiset of input magnitudes (and so |W| row sums), and every edge's Dale sign; only which same-kind type an input comes from is destroyed. The shuffle is redrawn per seed. Threshold: 0.5% of the control's pooled nats/char, fixed before any lab run.
